entry.label: Identity
entry.description: Identity is continuity through change, not the absence of change. It is enacted through boundaries, narratives, roles, purposes, memory and repeated relations.
entry.canonical_definition: A maintained pattern of distinctions, relationships and commitments through which a system remains recognisable across adaptation without requiring unchanging components.

profile.title: Identity
profile.canonical_definition: A maintained pattern of distinctions, relationships and commitments through which a system remains recognisable across adaptation without requiring unchanging components.
profile.summary: Identity is continuity through change, not the absence of change. It is enacted through boundaries, narratives, roles, purposes, memory and repeated relations.
profile.why_it_matters: Organisations can adapt so little that they cease to fit their environment, or change so incoherently that they can no longer say who they are. Viability needs both continuity and movement.
key_distinctions: identity of whole vs identities of parts
practice_connections: ask what must continue and what may change
compare official identity with repeated practice
look for identity conflict across levels
common_misreadings: a whole has only one identity
profile.editorial_note: Readable orientation and evidence-backed first pass. Named editorial review is still required before canonical acceptance.
